correctness.rationale: Exactly 2^16 incoming/outgoing bijection assignments exhaust the binary four-vertex-word de Bruijn digraph, and exactly 2048 single cycles remain. Independent edge-by-edge Eulerian DFS gives precisely the same cycle set. For every cycle, each length-1..19 circular factor is tested with both strict least-conjugate and strict least-proper-suffix Lyndon criteria. Both agree and give 2047 distinct signatures through length 18, with one identified doubleton, and 2048 through length 19; all rows are independently regenerated from the final package. The theorem is finite only, so no infinite-family assertion is inferred.

originality.rationale: Saari (arXiv:1207.4233) analyzes minimal Lyndon-factor counts and recurrence, not an exact de Bruijn reconstruction threshold. Goc–Saari–Shallit (arXiv:1207.5124) studies automatic and linearly recurrent sequences, not injective aggregate factor profiles on order-five de Bruijn cycles. Glen–Simpson–Smyth (arXiv:1701.00928) establishes unrestricted maximum/mean counts; positional-array reconstruction (Daykin et al., 2018) uses substantially richer data. Direct searches of mathematical publications and retrieved research findings gave no equivalent length-19 aggregate-count injectivity statement. Earlier unindexed results remain a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: Lyndon factor complexity is a natural invariant whose relationship with universal cycles is established by the classic Lyndon-concatenation construction. Ordinary factor-complexity counts cannot distinguish any order-five de Bruijn cycles, but the 14 aggregated Lyndon factor counts of lengths 6..19 distinguish all 2048. The uniquely colliding pair at length 18 certifies a mathematically sharp reconstruction threshold, a meaningful finite classification rather than a routine one-number enumeration. The exact fact supplies a benchmark for how much Lyndon-based factor information a universal cycle retains; no unproved generalization is claimed.
